finding.title: Override the injectable LocalDayClock in backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time assertions

evidence.quote: final now = DateTime.now(); / final lastSynced = now.subtract(const Duration(seconds: 30));

finding.why: _formatTimeAgo reads DateTimeFactory.nowLocal(), which resolves through the overridable localDayClockProvider — a FakeLocalDayClock already exists in lib/core/time/local_day_clock.dart for exactly this purpose. This file never overrides it: it seeds 'just now'/'Xm ago' assertions from real DateTime.now() at 5 call sites (lines 155, 179, 201, 227, 657), then the widget independently re-reads the clock a pump later. Today's margins (e.g. a 30s buffer under the 60s 'just now' cliff) make an actual flake unlikely, but the suite is non-deterministic by construction and the gap between test-now and widget-build-now is unbounded on a loaded/slow CI runner.
finding.recommendation: In _buildHarness, call useLocalDayClock(FakeLocalDayClock(fixedInstant)) (or override localDayClockProvider) and derive lastSynced from that same fixed instant, removing the wall-clock dependency entirely.
acceptance_criteria: backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time tests construct lastSyncedAt from a fixed instant and override localDayClockProvider/useLocalDayClock to that same instant.
The suite still passes with no bare DateTime.now() feeding a time-relative text assertion.

finding.title: outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider mutates DAO state and fires a network re-enqueue from inside its Provider build function
finding.why: The code directly inside `Provider<OutboxSyncWriteFacade?>((ref) {...})` mutates pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and unawaited-fires reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows(profileId) unconditionally on every build. This provider watches authStateProvider, activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider, userDatabaseProvider, activeProfileIdProvider, and localDayClockProvider -- any of which changing (e.g. every profile switch in this multi-child app) reruns build and refires the recovery scan, which its own D14 comment says is meant to run once. SM-2 exists precisely because 'side effects in build race and get skipped or duplicated on rebuild' -- here they duplicate on every rebuild instead of running once.
finding.recommendation: Move syncSink wiring and the one-time ledger-recovery call out of build into a ref.listen/onDispose pairing or an explicit one-shot recovery triggered on cloud-conversion, leaving build to only construct and return the facade.
acceptance_criteria: riverpod_lint/custom_lint rule flagging DAO field mutation or unawaited async calls directly inside a Provider build body (SM-2 Enforce backstop).
Regression test with a spy DAO asserting reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows is invoked at most once per profile per session, not once per rebuild (simulate two profile switches).

finding.title: onEnqueueDrain closures in sync_providers.dart read ref after an await with no ref.mounted guard
finding.why: Both onEnqueueDrain closures (in syncWriteFacadeProvider and outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider) do a ref.read after an await with no ref.mounted check, violating SM-4. Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException if ref is used after its provider has rebuilt. Both providers watch activeProfileIdProvider/authStateProvider, which change on every profile switch or sign-out -- realistic during the network round-trip a drain takes. If that happens between the two awaits, the second ref.read(syncOrchestratorProvider)?.recordDrainAttempt() throws on a stale ref. The surrounding comment (sync_providers.dart:100-104) spells out the user-visible cost of skipping recordDrainAttempt: 'the badge stays at its old value (e.g. a stale Synced) ... a false-Synced when the push failed.' Because this closure runs inside unawaited(tee().catchError((Object _) {})) in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart, the resulting exception is silently swallowed (see the companion EH-3 finding), so this failure currently has zero observability.
finding.recommendation: Check ref.mounted after the first await in both closures before the second ref.read call, per SM-4; extract the duplicated closure body into one shared helper to fix both sites at once.
acceptance_criteria: custom_lint/riverpod_lint rule flagging ref use after an await without a mounted check (SM-4 Enforce backstop).
Provider test that rebuilds/switches the active profile mid-drain and asserts no UnmountedRefException reaches the caller and recordDrainAttempt either completes or is safely skipped.

finding.title: OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue swallows every drain-tee failure with no log and no AppLogger field in the class
finding.why: OutboxSyncWriteFacade never declares an AppLogger field, so this catchError has no way to log even if it wanted to. Any exception from the drain tee -- including the UnmountedRefException from the companion SM-4 finding, or a genuine permission-denied/network failure -- is discarded with zero trace. Every push*/enqueue* method in this class, used for every sync write in the app, funnels through this one _enqueue, making it the single choke point where all fire-and-forget drain failures currently vanish silently. No test in this batch (including the 1184-line local_data_upload_service_test.dart, which never wires onEnqueueDrain) exercises this path either.
finding.recommendation: Inject an AppLogger into OutboxSyncWriteFacade (mirroring LocalDataUploadService's existing nullable _logger field) and log the swallowed exception at warn/error level inside catchError before discarding it.
acceptance_criteria: EH-3 Rule-0 checker (log-less catch grep) reports no hits in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart.
Unit test that stubs onEnqueueDrain to throw and asserts the logger receives the error.

finding.title: syncStatusProvider/syncStatusStreamProvider are duplicated verbatim between core/sync and features/sync -- the unread copy still needed its own bugfix

evidence.quote: // mirroring the core-layer canonical provider in

finding.why: sync_providers.dart's syncStatusStreamProvider/syncStatusProvider are byte-for-byte duplicates of lib/core/sync/providers/sync_status_providers.dart's providers of the same name (outside this batch); each file's doc comment calls the OTHER file canonical while neither actually delegates to the other -- two independent implementations. Grepping all 20 features-layer files that import sync_providers.dart for unrelated symbols (syncWriteFacadeProvider etc.) turns up zero uses of syncStatusProvider/syncStatusStreamProvider from this file; every real consumer (dashboard_screen.dart, backup_sync_section.dart) reads the core copy instead. The features copy is reachable only through its own 115-line dedicated regression test and the also-unreferenced SyncStatusIndicator widget. This is proven, not hypothetical, duplication cost: the 'loop-iter2' late-subscriber bug had to be fixed independently in both copies, exactly as the test file's own comment documents.
finding.recommendation: Delete syncStatusStreamProvider/syncStatusProvider from features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart; repoint SyncStatusIndicator and sync_status_provider_loading_state_test.dart at the core provider (or delete them per the companion dead-widget finding).
acceptance_criteria: AG-4 duplicate-symbol audit (orchestrator-level per digest) no longer lists syncStatusProvider/syncStatusStreamProvider twice.
grep confirms zero remaining declarations of these two names under lib/features/.
